data.narrative:
Lumotive is a Series B semiconductor company founded by Gleb Akselrod that has raised $72M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparison universe of 8 private peers and 3 public semiconductor companies (ALAB, NVDA, AMD), selected on sector alignment and stage proximity.

Two quantitative methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $72M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $137M. Peer-median benchmarking across 5 same-sector and same/adjacent-stage comparables (SambaNova Systems, Etched, d-Matrix, Positron AI, DEEPX) produces a $2.0B midpoint, with a range of $529M to $11.0B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples was not applicable because Lumotive's revenue is not on file; the public semiconductor sector median of 21.4x P/S cannot be applied absent the target's revenue disclosure.

The triangulation of these two methods supports a valuation range of $1.1B median, with a low bound of $116M and a high bound of $2.3B. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty: stage-progression and peer-median methods diverge substantially, suggesting sensitivity to stage classification and peer selection. Key unknowns include Lumotive's revenue traction, unit economics, and whether peers cited represent truly comparable market positioning within frontier semiconductor infrastructure.
